name: Grande Plage and the Centre
tagline: The Belle Epoque seafront, with the casino and the town beach
description: The heart of Biarritz around the main beach, the 1920s casino and the Hotel du Palais that Napoleon III built for Eugenie. The Halles market, the restaurants and the shops are a few streets back. It is the most expensive part of town and the reason most people come.
bestFor: Stays that want the town beach and the market within a five-minute walk
pros: The main beach and the promenade at the door
Halles market and the best restaurants nearby
cons: The highest rents on this coast
Very crowded from June to September

name: Cote des Basques
tagline: Below the cliff, where European surfing began
description: The long beach south of the centre under a green cliff, the break where surfing arrived in Europe in the 1950s and still the town's surf centre. Above it sit residential streets with sea views and the coast path towards the lighthouse. It is quieter than the Grande Plage and more committed.
bestFor: Anyone here to surf, with the break below the window
pros: The town's main surf break directly below
Cliff path and sea views along the whole street
Ten minutes on foot to the centre
cons: Steep access down to the beach
High rents for anything with a view
Beach disappears entirely at high tide

name: Saint-Charles and Beaurivage
tagline: Residential streets behind the coast, better value
description: The residential districts inland from the Cote des Basques, with ordinary apartment buildings and houses, local shops and a genuine year-round population rather than holiday lets. Rents drop noticeably as soon as you lose the sea view, and the centre remains a ten-minute walk.
bestFor: Longer stays that want a real neighbourhood at a rent below the seafront
pros: Meaningfully cheaper than anything on the coast
A neighbourhood that stays open in winter
Ten to fifteen minutes on foot to the beach
cons: No sea view and little charm
Uphill walk back from the beach

name: Anglet Chambre d'Amour
tagline: The next town north, long beaches and much lower rents
description: Anglet runs north from Biarritz along four kilometres of sand backed by a pine forest, with a string of surf beaches, a relaxed residential character and rents well below its famous neighbour. The tram-bus runs down the coast, and Bayonne is a few minutes inland.
bestFor: Surfers on a budget who want the same coast at a fraction of the Biarritz price
pros: Four kilometres of surf beach and pine forest behind
Rents well below Biarritz for equivalent flats
Frequent bus down the coast and to Bayonne
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes from central Biarritz
Beach car parks are a known target for break-ins

name: Bayonne Petit Bayonne
tagline: The real Basque town eight kilometres inland
description: Bayonne sits where the Nive meets the Adour, a proper Basque town of tall shuttered houses, the ham and chocolate trade, the cathedral and the July fetes. It has the region's best market and much cheaper rents than the coast, with a frequent train and bus link to Biarritz.
bestFor: Stays that want the Basque town and the market rather than the resort
pros: The best market and food culture in the region
Trains and buses to Biarritz every few minutes
cons: Very busy during the July fetes
